content: A hypnic jerk, also referred to as a hypnagogic jerk, is an involuntary muscle twitch that occurs during the transition into the hypnagogic state, which is the phase between wakefulness and sleep. This phenomenon is often described as resembling an electric shock or a sensation of falling, and it can result in sudden, noticeable movements of the body while lying in bed. Hypnic jerks are a common experience for most individuals, particularly when they are extremely fatigued or attempting to sleep in an uncomfortable position. These muscle twitches typically occur once or twice per night. However, during normal sleep, less intense and more regular hypnic jerks may also take place. In rare and extreme cases, frequent hypnic jerks may be classified as a sleep disorder known as periodic limb movement disorder (PLMD). Individuals with this condition often remain asleep and are unaware of the movements during the episodes. When a person is sleep-deprived and actively trying to resist falling asleep, hypnic jerks are more likely to occur. This is especially common in individuals who have been awake for more than 24 hours or those who have recently woken up after an insufficient amount of sleep.
